title: Finite-Tor domains for ordinary etale chart adjunctions
statement: Fix a field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$ and a prime $\ell\ne p$. All schemes below are separated and finite type over $k$, and all maps are $k$-morphisms [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. Let $A\to B$ be a unital map of finite commutative rings killed by powers of $\ell$, and choose $N=\ell^n\geq1$ annihilating both. On small ordinary etale sites use constant-ring module derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories] and $T_T=(-)_B=-\otimes^L_{A_T}B_T$ [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. Write $D^b_{ctf}$ for bounded constructible complexes of finite Tor amplitude, as in [det-sp-et-proet-adjunction-transfer], and $R_T(1)=\mu_{N,T}\otimes_{(\mathbf Z/N)_T}R_T$ for $R=A,B$ [lem-asd-finite-etale-twist-line]. Let $h:U\to V$ be separated of finite type, with a compactification whose middle scheme is in the standing setting. Let $F^{et}_{h,R}=Rr_{*,R}j_{!,R}$ for that compactification [def-amb-etale-compact-support]. Then $F^{et}_{h,R}$ preserves $D^b_{ctf}$ for $R=A,B$. For every standing scheme $T$, comparison inverse image $\nu_T^*$ gives an equivalence $D^b_{ctf}(T_{et},R)\simeq D^b_{ctf}(T_{proet},R)$ preserving and reflecting each Tor interval [det-pe-finite-tor-comparison-noetherian]. Its canonical tensor comparisons intertwine coefficient extension, inverse image, finite Tate tensor powers and shifts on these subcategories. In particular $T_T$ preserves $D^b_{ctf}$, and for any standing map $u:T'\to T$ and $a\geq0$, $b\in\mathbf Z$, the functor $u^*(-)(a)[b]$ preserves $D^b_{ctf}$.

proof.text: Every standing scheme is Noetherian: a field is Noetherian (its only ideals are zero and the unit ideal), and finite type over a Noetherian base implies Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. In particular it is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Every finite coefficient ring is Noetherian, since ascending chains of its ideals stabilize in its finite underlying set. For $R=A,B$ and $K\in D^b_{ctf}(T_{et},R)$, choose a Tor interval $[\alpha,\beta]$ with $\alpha\le\beta$. By [lem-sf-etale-flat-constructible] choose a representing complex $P$ of flat constructible $R_T$-modules, zero outside $[\alpha,\beta]$. It is K-flat by [lem-pc-bounded-above-flat-kflat-site]. We use this construction separately for each input; there is no assertion that one interval works for all inputs.

source.place: Tag 03TT, lemma-when-ctf; morphisms.tex Tag 01T6, lemma-finite-type-noetherian; sites-cohomology.tex Tag 06YQ, lemma-bounded-flat-K-flat

proof.text: Write the chosen compactification as $U\xrightarrow j\overline U\xrightarrow r V$. Apply the model of Step 1 on $U$. Extension by zero is exact and preserves quasi-isomorphisms by [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-exact], so $j_!P$ represents $Dj_!K$. Its terms are constructible by [lem-fin-extension-by-zero]. They are flat: for a module sheaf $M$ on $\overline U$, [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-slice-extension-tensor] gives $(j_!P^q)\otimes M\simeq j_!(P^q\otimes j^*M)$. Here restriction $j^*$ is exact by [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact]; tensoring with $P^q$ and applying $j_!$ are exact too. Thus the displayed functor of $M$ is exact. The complex $j_!P$ is still zero outside $[\alpha,\beta]$, and is K-flat by [lem-pc-bounded-above-flat-kflat-site]. Its tensor with any degree-zero module sheaf is therefore zero outside this interval. Its cohomology is constructible because kernels and cokernels of maps of constructible sheaves are constructible by [thm-constructible-serre]. Hence $Dj_!K$ lies in $D^b_{ctf}(\overline U_{et},R)$, with Tor interval $[\alpha,\beta]$.

source.place: Tags 03DJ, lemma-extension-by-zero-exact, and 0E8I, lemma-j-shriek-and-tensor; etale-cohomology.tex Tags 03S5 and 03RZ

proof.text: The map $r$ is proper and $V$ is quasi-compact. By [lem-sfb-finite-proper-geometric-cd-bound] there is $e\ge0$ such that all torsion abelian sheaves on all geometric fibres have cohomology zero above $2e$. This includes every $\ell$-power torsion sheaf, so it supplies precisely the fibre hypothesis of [det-ctf-finite-proper-tor], with $d=2e$. Both $\overline U,V$ and $r$ are in the standing setting by the hypothesis on the compactification. Applying that node to $Dj_!K$ from Step 2 gives $Rr_*Dj_!K\in D^b_{ctf}(V_{et},R)$, with Tor interval $[\alpha,\beta+2e]$. This is $F^{et}_{h,R}K$ by [def-amb-etale-compact-support]. Apply the same argument for $R=A$ and for $R=B$.

source.place: Tag 0F12, lemma-pull-out-constant-mod-n; proper finite-Tor application in det-ctf-finite-proper-tor; uniform fibre bound in lem-sfb-finite-proper-geometric-cd-bound

proof.text: For $K\in D^b_{ctf}(T_{et},A)$ choose $P$ as in Step 1. The change-of-rings functor of [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] is represented by $P\otimes_{A_T}B_T$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] to the identity topos with ring map $A_T\to B_T$: this complex is K-flat with flat $B_T$-terms. Each term is constructible. Indeed, on a stratum and an etale cover trivializing the constructible term $P^q$ as a finite $A$-module $M$, the extended term is the constant $B$-module $M\otimes_A B$. It is finite, being a quotient of a finite free $B$-module. The same strata therefore satisfy [def-weil-pbc-etale-constructible-sheaf] over $B$. This complex is still zero outside $[\alpha,\beta]$; kernels and cokernels are constructible by [thm-constructible-serre], and tensoring this flat model with any $B_T$-module stays in $[\alpha,\beta]$. Thus $T_TK\in D^b_{ctf}(T_{et},B)$, even when $B$ has infinite projective dimension over $A$.

source.place: Tag 03TT, lemma-when-ctf, and lemma-tensor-constructible (Tag 0GKB); sites-cohomology.tex Tags 06YY, 0G7E and 07A4

proof.text: For a standing map $u:T'\to T$, the constant-coefficient module inverse image is exact by [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact]. Hence applying it termwise to $P$ represents $u^*K$. Its terms are flat and K-flat as a complex by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. Constructibility of inverse images is [prop-constructible-pullback]; in the module formulation, pull back the local constant finite-module trivializations of [def-weil-pbc-etale-constructible-sheaf], with their scalar actions. Cohomology of the bounded resulting complex is constructible by [thm-constructible-serre]. It is zero outside $[\alpha,\beta]$, and its tensor with any degree-zero module sheaf is zero outside the same interval. Thus $u^*$ preserves $D^b_{ctf}$ and the chosen Tor bound.

source.place: Tag 03TT, lemma-when-ctf, and lemma-pullback-ctf; sites-modules.tex Tag 04JC; sites-cohomology.tex Tag 0G7E

proof.text: The integer $N=\ell^n$ is a unit on every standing scheme: its image in the characteristic-$p$ field is nonzero, so its inverse in $k$ maps to an inverse in every local ring. By [lem-asd-finite-etale-twist-line], $R_T(a)$ is a flat finite locally constant line for each $a\ge0$, including $R_T(0)=R_T$. It is constructible by the one-stratum case of [def-weil-pbc-etale-constructible-sheaf]. Tensor with this flat constructible sheaf preserves bounded constructibility by [lem-fd-flat-constructible-tensor]. It also preserves the Tor interval of $K$: tensor the model $P$ with the line. Each term is flat because tensoring with it is the composite of two exact tensor functors, and the complex has the same finite support and is K-flat by [lem-pc-bounded-above-flat-kflat-site]. For any integer $b$, shifting a model replaces its degree $q$ term by its degree $q+b$ term and changes the differential by $(-1)^b$; thus it changes $[\alpha,\beta]$ to $[\alpha-b,\beta-b]$ and retains constructibility and flatness. Combining this with Step 5 proves the assertion for $u^*(-)(a)[b]$.

source.place: Tags 03PK, section-kummer, 095I, lemma-tensor-product-constructible, and 0961, lemma-tensor-c; sites-cohomology.tex Tag 06YQ, lemma-bounded-flat-K-flat

proof.text: For each standing $T$ and $R=A,B$, $T$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated and $R$ is a discrete Noetherian ring by Step 1. Apply [det-pe-finite-tor-comparison-noetherian] with $X=T$ and $\Lambda=R$. It gives the required equivalence on $D^b_{ctf}$ and both implications for every Tor interval $[\alpha,\beta]$. No adjunction-transfer theorem is used to assert this equivalence or the preservation already proved in Steps 2--6.

source.place: Tag 09AL, lemma-compare-constructible-derived; the tensor-test preservation/reflection argument of det-pe-finite-tor-comparison-noetherian.proof.md

proof.text:
For coefficient change the comparison is the canonical isomorphism $
u_{T,B}^*(K\otimes^L_{A_T}B_T)\simeq(
u_{T,A}^*K)\otimes^L_{A_{T,proet}}B_{T,proet}$. To see this in the $B$-module category, use $P$ from Step 1: its extension is the flat model of Step 4, and both sides are represented by the termwise comparison $
u_T^{-1}(P^q\otimes_{A_T}B_T)\simeq
u_T^{-1}P^q\otimes_{
u_T^{-1}A_T}
u_T^{-1}B_T$. Constant ring identifications and exactness are [lem-sf-comparison-pullback-exact], and the canonical tensor comparison and preservation of K-flat flat-term representatives are [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. The map is $B$-linear since the scalar $b$ acts through the second tensor factor on both sides. Naturality of the cited tensor comparison gives naturality in $K$; this is the canonical comparison rather than an isomorphism chosen from the equivalence. Both objects are in the indicated subcategories by Steps 4 and 7.

source.place: Tag 07A4, lemma-pullback-tensor-product, and Tag 0G7E, lemma-pullback-K-flat; sites-modules.tex Tag 04JC

proof.text:
For scheme inverse image use the canonical natural comparison $
u_{T'}^*u_{et}^{-1}\simeq u_{proet}^{-1}
u_T^*$ of [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback]. It applies to module sheaves with the same finite constant scalar ring. Exactness of the etale inverse image is [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact], of the pro-etale coefficient pullback is [lem-pur-coefficient-pullback-exact], and of $
u^*$ is [lem-sf-comparison-pullback-exact]. Therefore the same comparison, applied termwise, is the derived comparison on $K$. Its isomorphism identifies the pro-etale pullback of $
u_T^*K$ with $
u_{T'}^*(u^*K)$, which lies in $D^b_{ctf}$ by Steps 5 and 7. The identity and composition compatibilities are already part of the statement of [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback].

For $m=N$ and $R=A,B$, [lem-amb-finite-root-site-comparison] identifies the etale root sheaf pulled to the pro-etale site with the same root functor there, sending a root to that same unit, and gives $
u_T^*R_T(1)\simeq R_{T,proet}(1)$. Apply the canonical tensor comparison [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] repeatedly to its $a$ tensor factors and to $K$; for $a=0$ use the constant unit identification of [lem-sf-comparison-pullback-exact]. This gives $
u_T^*(K(a))\simeq(
u_T^*K)(a)$ for every $a\ge0$. The root comparison is compatible with scheme pullback, as its cited statement explicitly asserts. Finally $
u^*$ is termwise exact by [lem-sf-comparison-pullback-exact], so it commutes with reindexing a cochain complex and its signed differential: $
u_T^*(K[b])\simeq(
u_T^*K)[b]$. Steps 6 and 7 put all these objects in $D^b_{ctf}$. Together with Steps 8--9 these are the asserted canonical intertwinings.

split_report.summary: Expanded the ordinary etale finite-Tor domain checks into ten steps. Reused existing bounded flat constructible models, open tensor/exactness, proper finite-Tor bounds, coefficient and inverse-image calculus, and the root-normalized site comparison. No new nodes and no change to the statement. Checked arbitrary finite rings and arbitrary standing fields; no flatness of A to B is assumed.
split_report.blueprint: det-sp-reduction-exceptional, Charts: the canonical isomorphism (e^*p_d^*K(d)[2d])_B ≃ e^*p_d^*(K_B)(d)[2d], and the finite-Tor domains needed to transfer that chart adjunction. Retains the ordinary etale route of the parent split.

tool_uses.why: Generic finite-type Noetherian permanence supplies the flat-model hypotheses.
Generic K-flat criterion computes tensors with the bounded models, on either small site.
Ordinary etale exact extension by zero computes the compactification functor.
Ordinary etale constructibility for terms extended from the open.
Generic ringed-site tensor identity proves flatness of extension by zero.
Ordinary constant-coefficient inverse image is exact, including restriction in the open-flatness calculation.
Kernels and cokernels of maps between the model terms retain constructibility.
Uniform all-torsion geometric fibre bound supplies the precise hypothesis of the proper finite-Tor theorem.
Proper finite-Tor theorem applies to the middle compactification map, after extension by zero.
General ringed-topos K-flat and canonical tensor calculus applies to scalar extension and both site inverse images.
Generic constructibility of pullback applies to the terms of the ordinary etale flat model.
Arbitrary finite-ring Tate lines, with N invertible, supply flat constructible twisting sheaves.
Flat constructible line tensor preserves bounded constructibility.
Existing site equivalence preserving and reflecting each Tor interval is used as a comparison tool.
Identifies constant scalar rings and the exact termwise site inverse image.
Canonical scheme inverse-image comparison, including its naturality and composition.
Exactness of the actual constant-ring pro-etale module inverse image.
Root-normalized ordinary etale/pro-etale Tate-line comparison for arbitrary finite rings.

The live item is still unsplit: Q13's FIX was refused at landing and Q63 was RETURNed, so this delivery is not superseded. There is no repair note, the statement is unchanged and nothing cites SGA. The off-chapter snapshot symlinks dangle, so I read those cited statements from the live tree. Step checks: (1) finite-type-over-Noetherian, then the flat constructible model of lem-sf-etale-flat-constructible (finite Λ, Noetherian X), made K-flat by the bounded-above-flat lemma. (2) j_! is exact, keeps terms constructible (lem-fin-extension-by-zero) and keeps them flat via the ringed-slice tensor identity; Serre gives constructible cohomology. (3) The geometric-fibre bound for every torsion sheaf gives d=2e for det-ctf-finite-proper-tor; Ū is standing by hypothesis; the interval is [α,β+2e]. (4) Change of rings on the K-flat model: flat terms by ringed-topoi pullback, constructible by local M⊗_A B, valid for Z/ℓ²→F_ℓ. (5) u* via exact inverse image, ringed-topoi flatness and constructible pullback. (6) N is invertible; the twist line is flat, locally free and constructible; lem-fd-flat-constructible-tensor applies; shift sign is right. (7) det-pe-finite-tor-comparison-noetherian with qcqs and Noetherian Λ. (8)-(10) Canonical comparisons: constant-ring identification, tensor comparison, comparison-pullback with identities and composites, and the root comparison σ_{N,T} with pullback compatibility (actual roots, not chosen trivializations). Edge cases checked: U empty, N=1, a=0, negative b, identity compactification. Advisory: Steps 1-4 re-prove inline the clauses of the existing node lem-sp-finite-compact-support-domains (split and reviewed, no cycle); there is no duplicate node, so this is not C5. Batch-5: the flagged det-ctf-finite-proper-tor reaches lem-trf-proper-finite-fibre-finite-near (finite fibre implies finite near a point) through the proper-constructibility chain. That is generic finiteness, which the trace formula assumes rather than proves, and it is not part of the proof of Poincaré duality; accepted.
